column1: Post-COVID Inflation & the Monetary Policy Dilemma: An Agent-Based Scenario Analysis

The thesis titled Post-COVID Inflation & the Monetary Policy Dilemma: An Agent-Based Scenario Analysis by Max Sina Knicker and colleagues explores the complex dynamics of inflation following the COVID-19 pandemic and the challenges faced by monetary policy in addressing these issues. The authors employ the Mark-0 Agent-Based Model to simulate the economic environment from 2020 to 2023  focusing on how economic agents  guided by behavioral rules  respond to various shocks. The study incorporates a mechanism that allows for the de-anchoring of trust in the Central Bank by economic agents.

The research investigates the impact of three significant exogenous shocks that occurred post-COVID: a production/consumption shock due to lockdowns  a supply-chain shock  and an energy price shock exacerbated by geopolitical tensions  specifically the Russian invasion of Ukraine. By analyzing these shocks under different assumptions about the effectiveness and transmission channels of monetary policy  the authors aim to understand the resurgence of inflation in the United States. They consider various factors such as demand-pull  cost-push  and profit-driven inflation.
The study's findings are fourfold: (i) without suitable fiscal policy interventions  the economy may take years to recover from these shocks or could even fall into a deep recession
column2: (ii) the success of monetary policy in controlling inflation is largely attributed to the anchoring of expectations rather than the direct economic impact of interest rate hikes
column3: (iii) strong inflation anchoring  while beneficial for controlling inflation  can negatively affect consumption and employment  creating a narrow window for optimal policy responses due to the trade-off between inflation and unemployment
column4: (iv) the model identifies wage and price indexation as the most sensitive parameters affecting inflation dynamics.

column1: These results have significant implications for Central Bank decision-making  providing a tool to anticipate the outcomes of different monetary and fiscal policies. The study emphasizes the importance of expectation management in monetary policy and highlights the delicate balance policymakers must maintain to stabilize inflation without adversely impacting economic growth and employment.
